'''Jesús Luis "Koldo" Álvarez de Eulate Güergue''' (born 4 September 1970) is a former [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]. He is currently [[Manager (association football)|manager]] of the [[Andorra national football team|Andorra national team]].

==Playing career==
Born in [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]], [[Álava]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Spain, Álvarez spent his entire career in the country.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://alaves.elcorreo.com/lecciones-alaves-principado-20221015191943-nt.html|title=Lecciones de un alavés en el Principado|trans-title=Lessons from an Álava man at the Principality|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|first=Jon|last=Aroca|language=es|date=15 October 2022|access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref> He signed in the 1990 summer [[transfer window]] with [[Atlético Madrid]] from local [[CD Aurrerá de Vitoria]], but struggled to appear even for [[Atlético Madrid B|the reserves]]. Due to injury to starter [[Abel Resino]], he was on [[Substitute (association football)|the bench]] for the first team in the [[1991 Copa del Rey final|final]] of the [[1990–91 Copa del Rey]], against [[RCD Mallorca]].<ref name=Cup>{{cite news|url=https://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/06/30/pagina-5/1230085/pdf.html|title=Fiesta rojiblanca en el Bernabéu|trans-title=Red-and-white party at the Bernabéu|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Tomás|last=Guasch|language=es|date=30 June 1991|access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

Álvarez resumed his career in the lower leagues, being second or third choice. In 1994, he joined [[FC Andorra]] who competed in the [[Spanish football league system]], going on to remain 14 of the following 15 seasons with the club and retiring aged 39.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/ser/2020/11/16/deportes/1605556500_045985.html|title=Los 'otros' españoles internacionales de la UEFA Nations League|trans-title=The 'other' Spanish internationals of the UEFA Nations League|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|first=Daniel|last=Plaza|language=es|date=16 November 2020|access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref> After being naturalised, he began representing the [[Andorra national football team|Andorra national team]], making his debut on 3 June 1998 in a 3–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] loss to [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/koldo-intl.html|title=Jesús Luis Alvarez de Eulate "Koldo" – International Appearances|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=Roberto|last=Mamrud|access-date=2 April 2021}}</ref>

On 10 June 2009, Álvarez played his last international, a 6–0 defeat against [[England national football team|England]] for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifiers]]; arguably one of the best players in the match, he received a standing ovation from the opposing fans for his efforts, after he was substituted in [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|injury time]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2009-06-10-3011605702_x.htm|title=Andorra loses 6–0 to England but prevents ridicule|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|first=Frank|last=Griffiths|date=10 June 2009|access-date=8 November 2010}}</ref> Previously, in November 2003, to celebrate [[UEFA]]'s Jubilee, he was selected as Andorra's [[UEFA Jubilee Awards|Golden Player]] by the [[Andorran Football Federation]] as their most outstanding player of the past 50 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.org/news/newsId=130150.html|title=Golden Players take centre stage|publisher=UEFA|date=29 November 2003|access-date=13 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/uefa-awards.html|title=Jubilee Awards|publisher=RSSSF|first1=Erik|last1=Garin|first2=Rui|last2=Silva|access-date=26 December 2011}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Álvarez was appointed as the Andorra national team's manager on 2 February 2010, replacing [[David Rodrigo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/esports/2010/02/02/koldo_nou_seleccionador_futbol_26221_1128.html|title=Koldo, nou seleccionador de futbol|trans-title=Koldo, new national team manager|newspaper=[[Diari d'Andorra]]|language=ca|date=2 February 2010|access-date=16 November 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208083242/https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/esports/2010/02/02/koldo_nou_seleccionador_futbol_26221_1128.html|archive-date=8 December 2022}}</ref> His first win (on his 49th game in charge) came seven years and 20 days later, 2–0 over [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] in a friendly.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/02/22/actualidad/1487795308_977481.html|title=Andorra derrota a San Marino y consigue su primera victoria en 13 años|trans-title=Andorra defeat San Marino and get their first win in 13 years|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Gorka|last=Pérez|language=es|date=22 February 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thesackrace.com/news/23rd-february-2017/koldo-alvarez-wins-first-andorra-match-at-49th-attempt|title=Koldo Alvarez wins first Andorra match at 49th attempt|publisher=The Sack Race|first=Jack|last=Kitson|date=23 February 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> 

On 25 March 2017, nearly 12 years after the last point won in official matches, Álvarez led the side to a 0–0 draw with [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2018 World Cup qualifying campaign]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/deportes/futbol/2017/03/25/58d6ddb722601d4b1f8b45f8.html|title=Y 58 partidos después, Andorra no perdió|trans-title=And 58 matches later, Andorra did not lose|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=25 March 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> On 9 June, for the same competition, a 1–0 win against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] in [[Andorra la Vella]] was achieved, the first competitive one since October 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/andorra/story/3141320/andorra-players-shed-tears-of-joy-after-first-competitive-win-since-2004|title=Andorra players shed tears of joy after first competitive win since 2004|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=9 June 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/06/10/andorra-stun-hungary-end66-match-winless-run-despite-completing/|title=Andorra stun Hungary to end 66-match winless run despite completing just 44 passes|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=10 June 2017|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Álvarez's son, [[Iker Álvarez|Iker]], is also a footballer and a goalkeeper. He was coached by his father in the national team setup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elperiodic.ad/entrevista/71045/lobjectiu-es-ser-porter-del-villarreal-i-acabar-jugant-a-la-primera-divisio|title="L'objectiu és ser porter del Villarreal i acabar jugant a la Primera Divisió"|trans-title="The goal is to be Villarreal's goalkeeper and end up playing in the First Division"|newspaper=[[El Periòdic d'Andorra]]|first=Miquel|last=López-Egea|language=ca|date=3 April 2019|access-date=28 March 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404132953/https://www.elperiodic.ad/entrevista/71045/lobjectiu-es-ser-porter-del-villarreal-i-acabar-jugant-a-la-primera-divisio|archive-date=4 April 2019}}</ref>
